name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q01 - Definition of reproductive health according to WHO

questiontext.text: According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), the term 'reproductive health' is comprehensively defined as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), reproductive health is not merely the absence of disease or having healthy organs with normal functions; it encompasses a broader perspective involving emotional, behavioural, and social dimensions.

Step 2: Evaluation
A reproductively healthy society consists of individuals who have physically and functionally normal reproductive organs and normal emotional and behavioural interactions among them in all sex-related aspects. Thus, it signifies total well-being across physical, emotional, behavioural, and social aspects of reproduction.

Step 3: Final Answer
Reproductive health represents total well-being in all aspects of reproduction, encompassing physical, emotional, behavioural, and social dimensions.

answer.text: A total well-being in all aspects of reproduction, including physical, emotional, behavioural, and social aspects
The physical presence of anatomically normal reproductive organs without regard to behavior
The complete absence of all sexually transmitted diseases in a given population
The capacity to reproduce successfully without requiring any medical intervention

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q02 - Year of initiating national family planning programmes

questiontext.text: In which year did India initiate national action plans and programmes towards attaining total reproductive health, popularly known as 'family planning'?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
India was amongst the first countries globally to initiate action plans and policies at a national level to attain total reproductive health as a social goal.

Step 2: Evaluation
These national action plans, known as 'family planning' programmes, were officially launched in the year 1951 and have been periodically reviewed and upgraded over the past decades into broader initiatives.

Step 3: Final Answer
The national family planning programmes in India were initiated in 1951.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q03 - Full name of RCH programmes in India

questiontext.text: Improved reproduction-related programmes currently in operation in India are popularly designated as 'RCH programmes'. What does RCH stand for?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Programmes covering wider reproduction-related aspects were implemented to replace and expand earlier family planning initiatives.

Step 2: Evaluation
The expanded programmes currently operating at the national level are known under the popular title 'Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes'. Their primary tasks include creating awareness and providing healthcare facilities to build a reproductively healthy society.

Step 3: Final Answer
RCH stands for Reproductive and Child Health Care.

answer.text: Regional Child Health Care
Reproductive and Community Hygiene
Reproductive and Child Health Care
Research in Child Health

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q04 - Statutory marriageable age for females and males

questiontext.text: As a legal measure to check rapid population growth in India, the statutory marriageable age has been fixed at:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Statutory raising of marriageable age is one of the legal interventions enforced to curb the rapid growth of population by ensuring biological and mental maturity before marriage.

Step 2: Evaluation
The legal minimum marriageable age established under statutory provisions in India is 18 years for females and 21 years for males.

Step 3: Final Answer
The statutory marriageable age in India is 18 years for females and 21 years for males.

answer.text: 21 years for females and 18 years for males
18 years for both females and males
21 years for both females and males
18 years for females and 21 years for males

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q05 - Premier institute that developed oral contraceptive Saheli

questiontext.text: The new oral contraceptive pill for females named 'Saheli' was developed by scientists at which research institute in India?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Research into improved and novel contraceptive agents has been supported by governmental bodies in India.

Step 2: Evaluation
'Saheli', a novel non-steroidal oral contraceptive pill taken once a week, was formulated and developed by scientists working at the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI) located in Lucknow, India.

Step 3: Final Answer
Saheli was developed at the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI) in Lucknow.

answer.text: Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow
National Institute of Immunology (NII), New Delhi
Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru
All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q06 - Identification of a nonmedicated intrauterine device

questiontext.text: Which of the following intra-uterine devices (IUDs) is categorised as a non-medicated IUD?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs) are broadly classified into non-medicated IUDs, copper-releasing IUDs, and hormone-releasing IUDs.

Step 2: Evaluation
Lippes loop is a classic non-medicated IUD. In contrast, CuT and Multiload 375 are copper-releasing IUDs, while LNG-20 is a hormone-releasing IUD.

Step 3: Final Answer
Lippes loop is the non-medicated intra-uterine device.

answer.text: CuT
Lippes loop
Multiload 375

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q07 - Classification of copper releasing intrauterine devices

questiontext.text: Which of the following intra-uterine devices is an example of a copper-releasing IUD?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Copper-releasing IUDs slowly diffuse copper ions inside the uterine cavity to suppress sperm motility and fertilising ability.

Step 2: Evaluation
Examples of copper-releasing IUDs include CuT, Cu7, and Multiload 375. Lippes loop is non-medicated, whereas Progestasert and LNG-20 are hormone-releasing.

Step 3: Final Answer
Multiload 375 is a copper-releasing intra-uterine device.

answer.text: Progestasert
Lippes loop
Multiload 375

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q08 - Popular brand of condom for the male

questiontext.text: Which of the following is a widely known and popular brand of condom for males supported and distributed in India?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Condoms are disposable barrier devices made of thin rubber or latex sheath used to prevent insemination during coitus.

Step 2: Evaluation
'Nirodh' is a popular and widely used brand of condom manufactured and marketed for males in India, providing barrier contraception and dual protection against sexually transmitted infections.

Step 3: Final Answer
Nirodh is the popular brand of condom for males.

answer.text: Saheli
Progestasert
Multiload
Nirodh

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q09 - Surgical sterilization procedure performed in male partners

questiontext.text: The surgical sterilisation procedure performed in males as a terminal method of contraception is known as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sterilisation techniques are terminal methods that surgically block gamete transport to prevent conception.

Step 2: Evaluation
The surgical sterilisation procedure in the male is termed vasectomy, wherein a small portion of the vas deferens is cut and ligated or tied up through a small scrotal incision. The female counterpart is tubectomy.

Step 3: Final Answer
The surgical sterilisation method in males is vasectomy.

answer.text: Vasectomy
Tubectomy
Laparoscopy
Hysterectomy

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q10 - Definition of medical termination of pregnancy

questiontext.text: Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) is scientifically defined as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Pregnancy termination may happen spontaneously or induced deliberately through clinical interventions.

Step 2: Evaluation
Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP), also referred to as induced abortion, is specifically defined as the intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full term.

Step 3: Final Answer
MTP is the intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full term.

answer.text: Spontaneous expulsion of an abnormal foetus during the third trimester
Intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full term
Surgical delivery of a baby by Caesarean section
Accidental miscarriage resulting from hormonal imbalance

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q11 - Primary diagnostic purpose of clinical amniocentesis

questiontext.text: What is the legitimate medical diagnostic purpose of the clinical procedure known as amniocentesis?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Amniocentesis involves taking a small sample of the amniotic fluid surrounding the developing foetus to culture and analyse fetal cells and dissolved biochemical substances.

Step 2: Evaluation
The medically legitimate purpose of this diagnostic technique is to detect chromosomal aberrations and genetic disorders (such as Down syndrome, haemophilia, and sickle-cell anemia) and assess fetal survivability.

Step 3: Final Answer
Amniocentesis is used to detect genetic disorders like Down syndrome, haemophilia, and sickle-cell anemia.

answer.text: Determining the sex of the foetus to satisfy parental curiosity
Inducing early uterine contractions to accelerate prolonged labour
Testing fetal cells and dissolved substances in amniotic fluid for genetic disorders such as Down syndrome, haemophilia, and sickle-cell anemia
Directly correcting metabolic defects inside the fetal liver in utero

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q12 - Legal ban on amniocentesis for sex determination

questiontext.text: Why has the Government of India imposed a statutory ban on the use of amniocentesis for sex determination?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Although developed as a diagnostic tool for genetic disorders, amniocentesis can also reveal the chromosomal sex of the fetus.

Step 2: Evaluation
The technique was frequently misused to detect the sex of the fetus, followed by induced abortion if the fetus was found to be female. To prevent this social menace of female foeticide, a strict statutory ban was enacted on its use for sex determination.

Step 3: Final Answer
The statutory ban was enacted to legally check and prevent female foeticide.

answer.text: Because amniotic fluid extraction invariably results in lethal physical damage to the mother
Because modern biochemical assays fail to determine chromosomal sex accurately
To promote surgical sterilisation among young pregnant women
To legally check the increasing menace of female foeticides resulting from prenatal sex determination

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q13 - Demographic factors contributing to Indian population explosion

questiontext.text: Which of the following sets of demographic changes represents the primary reasons for the dramatic surge in India's population during the last century?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Population explosion is triggered when birth and survival rates significantly exceed mortality rates across various cohorts.

Step 2: Evaluation
Better health facilities and living standards caused a rapid decline in the overall death rate, maternal mortality rate (MMR), and infant mortality rate (IMR). Concurrently, a larger proportion of individuals entered the reproducible age bracket, driving rapid population growth.

Step 3: Final Answer
Rapid decline in death rate, MMR, and IMR alongside an increase in people of reproducible age led to population explosion.

answer.text: Rapid decline in death rate, maternal mortality rate (MMR), and infant mortality rate (IMR), combined with an increase in individuals of reproducible age
Marked increase in infant mortality rate and maternal mortality rate coupled with decreased lifespan
Sharp reduction in people reaching reproducible age along with high immigration rates
Constant birth rate accompanied by an equally rising overall death rate

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q14 - Indian population growth rate in census report

questiontext.text: According to the 2011 census report, the annual population growth rate in India was recorded as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
National census reports provide official demographic figures on annual population growth rates and decadal growth rates.

Step 2: Evaluation
According to the 2011 census report, despite reproductive health initiatives, India's population growth rate stood at less than 2 per cent, which translates to approximately 20 per 1000 per year, a rate capable of causing rapid demographic expansion.

Step 3: Final Answer
The 2011 census reported an annual population growth rate of less than 2 per cent (20/1000/year).

answer.text: More than 5 per cent (50/1000/year)
Less than 2 per cent (20/1000/year)
Exactly 3.5 per cent (35/1000/year)
Around 0.2 per cent (2/1000/year)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q15 - Desirable characteristics of an ideal contraceptive method

questiontext.text: Which combination of properties accurately describes the requirements of an ideal contraceptive?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A contraceptive device is utilized to prevent conception without disrupting normal physiological or psychological well-being.

Step 2: Evaluation
An ideal contraceptive must be user-friendly, easily available, highly effective, completely reversible with no or minimal adverse side effects, and should in no way diminish or interfere with the sexual drive, desire, or act of the user.

Step 3: Final Answer
An ideal contraceptive must be user-friendly, easily available, effective, reversible, with least side effects, and non-interfering with sexual drive.

answer.text: Irreversible, expensive, completely suppresses natural sexual desire, and requires major hospital surgery
Highly effective, irreversible, and permanently terminating the menstrual cycle in females
User-friendly, easily available, effective, reversible, with no or least side-effects, and not interfering with sexual drive or act
Easily available, but causing moderate bleeding disturbances and suppressing libido

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q16 - Menstrual cycle period avoided in periodic abstinence

questiontext.text: In the natural contraceptive method known as periodic abstinence, why are couples advised to abstain from coitus from day 10 to day 17 of the menstrual cycle?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Natural contraceptive methods operate on the fundamental principle of avoiding the physical meeting of ovum and sperm.

Step 2: Evaluation
Ovulation occurs midway through the 28-day menstrual cycle (around day 14). Because ovum and sperm remain viable for a few days, days 10 to 17 represent the 'fertile period' where the probability of fertilisation is maximal. Abstaining from coitus during this window prevents conception.

Step 3: Final Answer
Days 10 to 17 constitute the fertile period when ovulation is expected and conception probability is highest.

answer.text: Because menstrual bleeding occurs throughout this time frame
Because cervical mucus becomes impenetrable to sperms exclusively during these days
Because the endometrial lining is completely shed during this phase
Because ovulation is expected during this fertile window, making chances of fertilisation very high

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q17 - Physiological principle and duration of lactational amenorrhea

questiontext.text: Which physiological principle underlies lactational amenorrhea, and what is its reported maximum period of contraceptive effectiveness?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Lactational amenorrhea relies on natural hormonal suppression of ovarian cycles during nursing.

Step 2: Evaluation
During the period of intense maternal lactation following parturition, high prolactin suppresses gonadotropin release, preventing ovulation and the menstrual cycle. This method carries almost zero side effects but is reported to be reliable only up to a maximum period of six months post-partum.

Step 3: Final Answer
Lactational amenorrhea depends on the absence of ovulation during intense lactation and is effective up to six months post-partum.

answer.text: Ovulation and menstruation do not occur during intense lactation following parturition; effective up to a maximum period of six months
High levels of progesterone destroy ejaculated sperms; effective up to one month post-partum
Oxytocin secretion physically blocks the cervical canal; effective up to twelve months
Breastfeeding causes permanent atrophy of ovarian follicles; effective for three years

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q18 - Contraceptive mechanism of copper releasing intrauterine devices

questiontext.text: What is the primary mode of action of copper-releasing IUDs (e.g., CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) in preventing pregnancy?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Intrauterine devices elicit a localized foreign body reaction in the endometrium while medicated variants release active agents.

Step 2: Evaluation
In the uterus, IUDs stimulate phagocytosis of spermatozoa by uterine leukocytes. Furthermore, copper ions continuously released from copper-bearing IUDs directly suppress sperm motility and inhibit their fertilising capability.

Step 3: Final Answer
Copper-releasing IUDs enhance uterine phagocytosis of sperms while released copper ions suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity.

answer.text: They completely suppress the secretion of FSH and LH from the anterior pituitary gland
They increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus, and released copper ions suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity
They induce immediate shedding of the endometrium every seven days
They cause permanent surgical occlusion of the fallopian tubes

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q19 - Functional mechanism of hormone releasing intrauterine devices

questiontext.text: In addition to increasing sperm phagocytosis, how do hormone-releasing IUDs (such as Progestasert and LNG-20) act to prevent conception?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hormone-releasing IUDs slowly discharge progestogens locally into the endometrial microenvironment.

Step 2: Evaluation
The sustained local presence of progestogen alters endometrial histology, rendering the uterus unsuitable for blastocyst implantation. Additionally, it thickens cervical mucus, making the cervix hostile and impenetrable to ascending spermatozoa.

Step 3: Final Answer
Hormone-releasing IUDs make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and render the cervix hostile to sperms.

answer.text: They destroy the Graafian follicles surgically upon contact
They prevent the release of seminal fluid in the male partner
They make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and render the cervix hostile to sperms
They act as external mechanical barriers over the vaginal orifice

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q20 - Identification of hormone releasing intrauterine contraceptive devices

questiontext.text: Which pair of intra-uterine devices belongs exclusively to the hormone-releasing category?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
IUDs are segregated by their functional composition: non-medicated, copper-bearing, and hormone-bearing.

Step 2: Evaluation
Progestasert and LNG-20 are both hormone-releasing IUDs that release synthetic progestogens. In contrast, CuT, Cu7, and Multiload 375 are copper-releasing, while Lippes loop is non-medicated.

Step 3: Final Answer
Progestasert and LNG-20 are hormone-releasing IUDs.

answer.text: Multiload 375 and CuT
Lippes loop and Cu7
CuT and Progestasert
Progestasert and LNG-20

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q21 - Administration schedule of conventional oral contraceptive pills

questiontext.text: What is the standard administration schedule for conventional combined oral contraceptive pills?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Oral contraceptive pills contain low doses of progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combinations.

Step 2: Evaluation
The pills are taken daily for a duration of 21 days, commencing preferably within the first five days of the menstrual cycle. This is followed by a 7-day gap during which withdrawal menstrual bleeding takes place, after which the 21-day cycle is repeated.

Step 3: Final Answer
Pills are taken daily for 21 days starting within the first 5 days of the cycle, followed by a 7-day pill-free gap.

answer.text: Taken daily for 21 days starting within the first 5 days of the menstrual cycle, followed by a 7-day pill-free interval
Taken once a week continuously without any pill-free interval
Taken daily for 7 days during menstrual flow, followed by 21 days of abstinence
Taken only within 72 hours following sexual intercourse as a single dose

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q22 - Structural nature and dosing pattern of Saheli

questiontext.text: Which statement correctly describes the unique pharmacological characteristics and dosing schedule of the oral contraceptive 'Saheli'?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Unlike conventional oral pills containing steroid hormones, Saheli represents a distinctive class of non-steroidal selective estrogen receptor modulators.

Step 2: Evaluation
Saheli contains a non-steroidal preparation. It is formulated as a 'once a week' oral pill with minimal side effects and high contraceptive efficacy, making it well-accepted among female users.

Step 3: Final Answer
Saheli is a non-steroidal, once-a-week oral contraceptive pill with minimal side effects.

answer.text: It is a high-dose steroid formulation taken twice daily for 21 days
It contains a non-steroidal preparation taken as a once-a-week pill with very few side effects
It is a subcutaneous steroid implant effective continuously for five years
It is an injectable progestogen administered once every three months

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q23 - Window and modalities used for emergency contraception

questiontext.text: To prevent possible pregnancy following casual unprotected coitus or rape, emergency contraceptives must be administered within what maximum timeframe, and using which agents?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Emergency contraception provides a post-coital intervention to disrupt fertilisation or prevent implantation before early embryogenesis is established.

Step 2: Evaluation
Administration of progestogens alone, progestogen-estrogen combinations, or insertion of IUDs within 72 hours of unprotected sexual intercourse has been proven to be highly effective as emergency contraception.

Step 3: Final Answer
Emergency contraceptives must be administered within 72 hours of coitus using progestogens, progestogen-estrogen combinations, or IUDs.

answer.text: Within 24 hours only, using high-dose broad-spectrum antibiotics
Within 7 days of coitus, using surgical sterilisation methods
Within 72 hours of coitus, using progestogens, progestogen-estrogen combinations, or IUDs
Within 14 days of coitus, using non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q24 - Anatomical modification performed during female tubectomy procedure

questiontext.text: Which surgical step is carried out during female sterilisation (tubectomy) to achieve permanent contraception?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Tubectomy is a surgical sterilisation procedure in females that physically blocks ovum transit down the fallopian tubes.

Step 2: Evaluation
In tubectomy, a small segment of each fallopian tube is surgically removed or tied up via a minor incision in the abdomen or through the vagina. This prevents the transported ovum from meeting spermatozoa.

Step 3: Final Answer
Tubectomy involves removing or tying up a small portion of the fallopian tubes.

answer.text: Both ovaries are completely excised to stop gametogenesis permanently
The uterine cavity is chemically ablated to prevent blastocyst attachment
A small portion of the vas deferens is cut and ligated through a scrotal incision
A small part of each fallopian tube is removed or tied up through a small incision in the abdomen or vagina

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q25 - Characteristics of female reusable barrier contraceptive methods

questiontext.text: Which of the following characteristics accurately describes female barrier devices such as diaphragms, cervical caps, and vaults?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Female barrier methods physically prevent ejaculated spermatozoa from entering the upper reproductive tract through the cervix.

Step 2: Evaluation
Diaphragms, cervical caps, and vaults are rubber barrier devices placed into the female tract to cover the cervix during coitus. Unlike condoms, they are reusable. Spermicidal creams, jellies, and foams are frequently applied alongside them to increase contraceptive efficiency.

Step 3: Final Answer
Diaphragms, cervical caps, and vaults are reusable rubber barriers covering the cervix, often used with spermicides.

answer.text: They are rubber devices inserted to cover the cervix, are reusable, and are commonly used with spermicidal creams
They are single-use disposable devices made of thin latex that cover the external vulva completely
They are surgically implanted into the uterine myometrium by a qualified doctor
They continuously release steroid hormones into circulation to prevent follicular ovulation

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q26 - Year of legalization of MTP in India

questiontext.text: In which year did the Government of India legalise Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) with strict conditions to prevent its misuse?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Legalisation of medical termination of pregnancy was enacted to curb illegal and hazardous abortion practices while imposing checks against its misuse.

Step 2: Evaluation
The Government of India officially legalised Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) under strict statutory guidelines in 1971 to prevent indiscriminate unsafe abortions and female foeticide.

Step 3: Final Answer
MTP was legalised in India in the year 1971.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q27 - Gestational period considered safe for performing MTP

questiontext.text: During which gestational period is Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) medically considered relatively safe for the mother?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The maternal risks associated with induced abortion increase considerably as the foetus enlarges and maternal-fetal vascular connections become extensive.

Step 2: Evaluation
MTP is considered relatively safe during the first trimester, which spans up to 12 weeks of pregnancy. Abortions performed during the second trimester carry far higher maternal health risks and surgical complications.

Step 3: Final Answer
MTP is relatively safe during the first trimester, up to 12 weeks of gestation.

answer.text: During the second trimester, between 13 and 24 weeks of pregnancy
During the third trimester, between 25 and 36 weeks of pregnancy
During the first trimester, up to 12 weeks of pregnancy
Only during the final month of gestation immediately preceding labor

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q28 - Medical practitioner opinion requirements under MTP Act

questiontext.text: Under the MTP (Amendment) Act, 2017, how many registered medical practitioners must form an opinion in good faith to terminate a pregnancy lasting between 12 and 24 weeks?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The MTP (Amendment) Act, 2017 specifies statutory regulations and medical consensus thresholds based on gestational age.

Step 2: Evaluation
A pregnancy within the first 12 weeks may be terminated on the opinion of one registered medical practitioner. However, if the pregnancy has lasted more than 12 weeks but fewer than 24 weeks, two registered medical practitioners must independently form an opinion in good faith that eligible statutory grounds exist.

Step 3: Final Answer
Two registered medical practitioners are required for pregnancies between 12 and 24 weeks.

answer.text: One registered medical practitioner
Four registered medical practitioners
A panel comprising five district health officers
Two registered medical practitioners

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q29 - Sexually transmitted infections that are not curable

questiontext.text: Which trio of sexually transmitted infections cannot be completely cured even if detected early and treated properly?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Most bacterial and protozoan sexually transmitted infections respond effectively to specific antimicrobial therapy when caught early.

Step 2: Evaluation
Except for Hepatitis-B, genital herpes, and HIV infection, other STIs (such as gonorrhoea, syphilis, chlamydiasis, genital warts, and trichomoniasis) are completely curable if detected at an early stage and properly treated.

Step 3: Final Answer
Hepatitis-B, genital herpes, and HIV infection are not completely curable.

answer.text: Hepatitis-B, genital herpes, and HIV infection
Gonorrhoea, syphilis, and chlamydiasis
Genital warts, trichomoniasis, and syphilis
Chlamydiasis, gonorrhoea, and trichomoniasis

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q30 - Non-sexual modes of transmission for HIV Hepatitis

questiontext.text: Apart from sexual intercourse, which other routes of transmission are common to both Hepatitis-B and HIV?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Blood-borne pathogens can pass between individuals through parenteral exposure and vertical transmission.

Step 2: Evaluation
Both Hepatitis-B virus and Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) are transmitted by sharing unsterilised injection needles or surgical instruments with infected persons, receiving contaminated blood transfusions, and vertically from an infected mother to her developing foetus.

Step 3: Final Answer
Hepatitis-B and HIV are transmitted via shared needles, surgical instruments, blood transfusion, and maternal-fetal transfer.

answer.text: Inhaling aerosol droplets produced during coughing or sneezing
Sharing injection needles or surgical instruments, blood transfusion, and transmission from infected mother to foetus
Consumption of contaminated food items and municipal drinking water
Bites by female Anopheles mosquitoes and houseflies

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q31 - Severe long-term clinical complications of untreated STIs

questiontext.text: Untreated sexually transmitted infections can progress and cause which group of severe clinical complications later in life?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Persistent genital tract infections trigger chronic inflammation and tissue scarring within pelvic reproductive anatomy.

Step 2: Evaluation
Failure to obtain timely treatment for STIs can lead to ascending pelvic inflammatory diseases (PID), spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, ectopic pregnancies (implantation outside the uterine cavity), secondary infertility, and even cancers of the reproductive tract.

Step 3: Final Answer
Untreated STIs lead to PID, abortions, stillbirths, ectopic pregnancies, and infertility.

answer.text: Cystic fibrosis, sickle-cell anemia, and muscular dystrophy
Type 1 diabetes, pancreatitis, and pulmonary emphysema
Pelvic inflammatory diseases (PID), abortions, stillbirths, ectopic pregnancies, and infertility
Myasthenia gravis, osteomalacia, and rickets

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q32 - Demographic age cohort most vulnerable to STIs

questiontext.text: Epidemiological data highlighted in NCERT indicates that incidences of sexually transmitted infections are reported to be exceptionally high in which age group?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Susceptibility to sexually transmitted infections is influenced by behavioral factors, lack of awareness, and sexual activity trends across demographics.

Step 2: Evaluation
Although individuals of all age groups can contract STIs, epidemiological reports emphasize that the incidence of STIs is disproportionately high among young persons in the age group of 15 to 24 years.

Step 3: Final Answer
The age group of 15 to 24 years is reported to have the highest incidence of STIs.

answer.text: 35 to 45 years
45 to 60 years
5 to 14 years
15 to 24 years

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q33 - Embryonic stage and site transferred in ZIFT

questiontext.text: In an assisted reproductive programme involving ZIFT (Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer), which entity is transferred and to which anatomical site?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In vitro fertilisation (IVF) is coupled with embryo transfer (ET) where the transfer location depends strictly on the developmental stage of the embryo.

Step 2: Evaluation
In Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer (ZIFT), the zygote or an early cleavage-stage embryo containing up to 8 blastomeres is transferred directly into the fallopian tube to complete natural transit and development.

Step 3: Final Answer
ZIFT transfers a zygote or early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube.

answer.text: A zygote or early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres is transferred into the fallopian tube
An embryo with more than 8 blastomeres is transferred into the uterine cavity
An unfertilised ovum along with donor semen is placed directly into the vagina
A blastocyst containing 64 cells is embedded surgically into the ovary

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q34 - Destination of embryos with over eight blastomeres

questiontext.text: In test tube baby programmes, embryos cultured to a developmental stage with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into the:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Embryos at more advanced cleavage stages naturally correspond to the uterine phase of development in vivo.

Step 2: Evaluation
While early embryos (up to 8 blastomeres) are introduced into the fallopian tube (ZIFT), embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred directly into the uterus (Intra Uterine Transfer - IUT) for subsequent implantation and gestation.

Step 3: Final Answer
Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into the uterus via Intra Uterine Transfer (IUT).

answer.text: Fallopian tube, a procedure designated as GIFT
Uterus, a procedure known as Intra Uterine Transfer (IUT)
Cervical canal, a procedure termed artificial insemination
Peritoneal cavity, a procedure known as laparoscopy

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q35 - Assisted reproductive technology suitable for anovulatory women

questiontext.text: A female patient is diagnosed with anovulation and cannot produce functional ova, but her reproductive tract, fallopian tubes, and uterus are healthy and capable of supporting fertilisation and embryonic development. Which assisted reproductive technique is most suitable for her?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Different assisted reproductive techniques address distinct physiological barriers in infertile individuals.

Step 2: Evaluation
In Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer (GIFT), an ovum harvested from a healthy donor is transferred into the fallopian tube of a recipient female who cannot generate her own ovum, but can provide a suitable physiological environment for in vivo fertilisation and subsequent development. Artificial insemination only introduces sperm, and ZIFT requires laboratory fertilisation first.

Step 3: Final Answer
Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer (GIFT) is the technique designed for anovulatory females with functional fallopian tubes.

answer.text: Intra Uterine Insemination (IUI)
Artificial Insemination (AI)
Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer (GIFT)
Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer (ZIFT) using her own unfertilised ovum

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q36 - Distinctive laboratory mechanism of intra cytoplasmic sperm injection

questiontext.text: What distinct laboratory micro-manipulation distinguishes Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) from conventional in vitro fertilisation (IVF)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Specialised assisted reproductive techniques are employed when spermatozoa fail to penetrate the egg's outer protective vestments spontaneously.

Step 2: Evaluation
In standard IVF, eggs and sperms are co-incubated to allow natural penetration. In Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI), specialised micromanipulators are used to inject a single viable sperm directly into the cytoplasm of an oocyte in vitro, forming an embryo under laboratory conditions.

Step 3: Final Answer
ICSI involves the direct micro-injection of a single sperm into the ovum's cytoplasm.

answer.text: Sperms and ova are simply co-incubated in a culture dish to allow spontaneous penetration
Spermatozoa are chemically treated to dissolve the outer follicular cells before vaginal delivery
Multiple sperms are placed inside the amniotic sac of a pregnant female
A single sperm is directly micro-injected into the cytoplasm of an ovum to achieve fertilisation in the laboratory

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q37 - Assisted reproductive method indicated for severe male oligospermia

questiontext.text: An infertile couple seeks medical guidance. Diagnostic evaluation reveals normal ovulatory cycles in the female partner, but the male partner suffers from severe oligospermia (very low sperm count) and inability to inseminate during coitus. Which clinical technique is indicated?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Male-factor infertility stemming from failure of coital deposition or subnormal sperm concentrations requires assisted semen introduction.

Step 2: Evaluation
When infertility arises from the inability of the male partner to inseminate or due to very low sperm counts (oligospermia), Artificial Insemination (AI) is utilized. In this technique, semen collected from the husband or a donor is processed and artificially introduced either into the vagina or into the uterus (Intra-Uterine Insemination - IUI).

Step 3: Final Answer
Artificial Insemination (AI) or Intra-Uterine Insemination (IUI) is indicated for oligospermia or failure of insemination.

answer.text: Artificial Insemination (AI) / Intra-Uterine Insemination (IUI)
Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer (GIFT) using only the patient's own unassisted coitus
Amniocentesis followed by hormone administration
Tubectomy followed by natural conception

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q38 - Matching contraceptive modalities with their primary mechanisms

questiontext.text:
Match the contraceptive methods in List I with their primary modes of action in List II:
List I: (P) CuT, (Q) LNG-20, (R) Combined oral pill, (S) Diaphragm
List II:
1. Blocks sperm entry through the cervix mechanically
2. Suppresses sperm motility and fertilising capacity
3. Inhibits ovulation and alters cervical mucus quality
4. Renders uterus unsuitable for implantation and cervix hostile to sperms

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Different contraceptive devices operate via mechanical, biochemical, or endocrine pathways to prevent fertilisation or implantation.

Step 2: Evaluation
CuT releases copper ions that suppress sperm motility and fertilising ability. LNG-20 is a hormone-releasing intra-uterine device that renders the uterus unsuitable for implantation and makes the cervix hostile to sperms. Combined oral contraceptive pills prevent ovulation and alter cervical mucus quality. Diaphragms are mechanical barriers placed over the cervix to block sperm entry.

Step 3: Final Answer
Copper IUDs suppress sperm motility, LNG-20 makes the uterus unsuitable for implantation, oral pills inhibit ovulation, and diaphragms physically block sperm entry through the cervix.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q39 - Triad of physiological mechanisms mediating oral contraceptive pills

questiontext.text: Combined oral contraceptive pills containing progestogen and estrogen prevent conception through which synergistic physiological triad?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Oral contraceptive formulations exert multi-target endocrine actions across the female reproductive axis.

Step 2: Evaluation
The progestogen-estrogen combination operates via three complementary actions: firstly, negative feedback on pituitary gonadotropins to inhibit ovulation; secondly, alteration of the endometrial architecture to inhibit blastocyst implantation; and thirdly, thickening and alteration of cervical mucus to impede and retard sperm entry into the uterine cavity.

Step 3: Final Answer
Pills prevent conception by inhibiting ovulation, inhibiting implantation, and altering cervical mucus to impede sperm entry.

answer.text: Lysis of mature spermatozoa in the vagina, destruction of corpus luteum, and tubal ligation
Permanent destruction of primary oocytes, induction of lactation, and cervical closure
Inhibition of ovulation, inhibition of blastocyst implantation, and alteration of cervical mucus quality to retard sperm entry
Phagocytosis of zygotes in the peritoneal cavity, suppression of oxytocin, and follicle stimulation

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q40 - Statutory grounds permissible for pregnancy termination under law

questiontext.text: According to the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act, 2017 in India, which of the following grounds constitutes a valid statutory justification for terminating a pregnancy?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The MTP (Amendment) Act, 2017 establishes precise legal, ethical, and medical parameters under which induced abortions can be performed.

Step 2: Evaluation
The legal grounds require that registered medical practitioners form an opinion in good faith that: (i) continuation of pregnancy would involve risk to the pregnant woman's life or grave injury to her physical or mental health; or (ii) there is substantial risk that if born, the child would suffer from physical or mental abnormalities causing serious handicap.

Step 3: Final Answer
Valid grounds require risk to the woman's life or health, or substantial risk of severe handicap in the child.

answer.text: Parental desire to balance family gender based on fetal karyotyping
Termination sought purely due to minor nausea or voluntary domestic lifestyle preference
Social pressure from relatives regarding the astrological birth date of the offspring

Continuation of pregnancy involves risk to the life of the pregnant woman or of grave injury to her physical or mental health, or substantial risk of serious physical or mental handicap to the unborn child

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q41 - Clinical implications of asymptomatic sexually transmitted infections females

questiontext.text: Why do sexually transmitted infections (STIs) in females often remain undetected for prolonged periods, and what serious anatomical consequence can arise from this delay?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The anatomical location and internal mucosal environment of the female reproductive tract often mask early signs of microbial colonization.

Step 2: Evaluation
Early symptoms such as slight itching, discharge, or minor pain are easily missed, and infected females are often completely asymptomatic. Combined with social stigma, this leads to long delays in diagnosis, allowing pathogens to ascend and cause pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), tubal scarring, ectopic pregnancy, and permanent infertility.

Step 3: Final Answer
Asymptomatic presentation in females delays detection, leading to severe complications like pelvic inflammatory disease.

answer.text: Infected females are frequently asymptomatic or show only minor early symptoms, leading to delayed diagnosis and chronic pelvic inflammatory disease (PID)
The female immune response instantly destroys all venereal bacteria, preventing symptomatic presentation
STIs in females are restricted exclusively to keratinized external skin and never reach internal organs
Females produce high levels of circulating antibodies that eliminate the need for clinical intervention

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q42 - Physiological endocrine mechanism underlying post partum lactational amenorrhea

questiontext.text: What is the underlying neuro-endocrine mechanism responsible for the temporary absence of ovulation during lactational amenorrhea?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The suckling stimulus by the infant triggers neural signals that alter hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis signaling.

Step 2: Evaluation
Intense lactation is driven by elevated prolactin. High prolactin levels suppress the pulsatile release of Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH) from the hypothalamus. Consequently, pituitary secretion of Follicle-Stimulating Hormone (FSH) and Luteinizing Hormone (LH) drops below the threshold required for follicular recruitment and ovulatory surge, resulting in amenorrhea.

Step 3: Final Answer
Suckling-induced prolactin suppresses hypothalamic GnRH, preventing gonadotropin release and subsequent ovulation.

answer.text: High levels of maternal estrogen stimulate excessive LH surges that permanently luteinize immature follicles
Intense suckling stimulates high prolactin release, which suppresses hypothalamic GnRH secretion, thereby inhibiting pituitary LH and FSH release necessary for ovulation
Oxytocin directly induces apoptosis of all primary oocytes within both ovaries
Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) remains persistently elevated, suppressing the ovarian cycle

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q43 - Physiological status of gametogenesis following surgical sterilization

questiontext.text: Following a successful surgical sterilisation procedure (vasectomy in a male or tubectomy in a female), what is the fate of gamete production and sex steroid secretion?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sterilisation techniques target gamete transport ducts rather than the primary gonadal endocrine and germinal tissues.

Step 2: Evaluation
In vasectomy, the testes remain intact and continue normal spermatogenesis and testosterone secretion; only sperm transit through the vas deferens is interrupted. In tubectomy, the ovaries continue normal oogenesis and cyclic estrogen/progesterone synthesis; only ovum transit along the fallopian tubes is blocked.

Step 3: Final Answer
Gametogenesis and steroid hormone secretion continue unimpaired, while gamete transport is physically interrupted.

answer.text: Gamete formation ceases immediately because gonadal blood supply is permanently severed
Sex steroid production halts completely, leading to the rapid loss of secondary sexual characteristics
Gametogenesis and sex hormone production continue normally, but gamete transport through the reproductive conduits is physically blocked
The gonads rapidly undergo complete fibrous atrophy and degenerate within weeks

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q44 - Origin of embryos utilized in assisted reproductive transfers

questiontext.text: In assisted reproductive technology programmes aimed at helping females who cannot conceive, what can be the biological origin of embryos used for transfer into the recipient?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Embryo transfer protocols can assist females with hostile tubal or uterine environments regardless of whether fertilisation occurred in vitro or in vivo.

Step 2: Evaluation
As explicitly detailed in NCERT, embryos transferred to assist females who cannot conceive can be produced either via in vitro fertilisation (fusion of gametes in the laboratory) or via in vivo fertilisation (natural fusion of gametes within a fertile donor female, followed by recovery and transfer).

Step 3: Final Answer
Embryos used for transfer may originate from either in vitro fertilisation or in vivo fertilisation.

answer.text: Embryos must strictly be formed by in vitro fertilisation, as in vivo embryos cannot survive transfer
Embryos must be formed exclusively by parthenogenesis without paternal genetic input
Embryos can only be obtained through somatic cell nuclear cloning of the recipient's cells
Embryos may be generated either by in vitro fertilisation (IVF) in the laboratory or by in vivo fertilisation followed by transfer from a fertile female donor

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q45 - Evaluation of statements concerning diverse intrauterine contraceptive devices

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs):
I. They must be inserted by qualified doctors or expert nurses into the uterus through the vagina.
II. Copper ions released from copper IUDs suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity.
III. Hormone-releasing IUDs make the cervix hostile to sperms and the uterus unsuitable for implantation.
IV. Lippes loop is an example of a copper-releasing IUD.
Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Intra Uterine Devices require clinical insertion and operate through category-specific biological mechanisms.

Step 2: Evaluation
Intra Uterine Devices must be placed by qualified medical professionals or nurses into the uterus through the vagina. Copper ions released by copper-bearing IUDs suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity. Hormone-releasing IUDs make the cervix hostile to sperms and render the uterus unsuitable for blastocyst implantation. Lippes loop is a non-medicated IUD made of plastic, not a copper-releasing device.

Step 3: Final Answer
Professional insertion, suppression of sperm motility by copper ions, and cervical hostility by hormones are valid characteristics, whereas Lippes loop is a non-medicated device.

answer.text: Statements I, II, and III only
Statements I, III, and IV only
Statements II and IV only
All four statements (I, II, III, and IV)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q46 - Demographic trends and census data of Indian population

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following statements regarding population trends in India:
I. India's population was approximately 350 million at independence and crossed 1.2 billion in May 2011.
II. A decline in death rate, maternal mortality rate (MMR), and infant mortality rate (IMR) contributed to explosive growth.
III. The 2011 census reported an annual growth rate of less than 2 per cent.
IV. The RCH programme brought about a massive, drastic reduction in the population growth rate to zero.
Which statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Demographic history reflects post-independence population growth dynamics and healthcare program impacts.

Step 2: Evaluation
India's population expanded from approximately 350 million at independence to cross 1.2 billion in May 2011. Rapid declines in death rate, maternal mortality rate (MMR), and infant mortality rate (IMR), coupled with an increased reproductive-age population, accelerated this surge. The 2011 census recorded an annual growth rate under 2 per cent (20 per 1000 per year). However, the RCH programmes achieved only a marginal reduction in population growth rather than bringing it to zero.

Step 3: Final Answer
Historical growth from 350 million to 1.2 billion, declines in maternal and infant mortality rates, and a census growth rate under 2 per cent are factually true, whereas population growth was not reduced to zero.

answer.text: Statements II, III, and IV only
Statements I, II, and III only
Statements I and IV only
All four statements (I, II, III, and IV)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q47 - Medical cautions and adverse effects of synthetic contraceptives

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements represents an accurate clinical perspective regarding the use and potential side effects of contraceptive methods?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Contraceptive intervention opposes a normal physiological event (conception) rather than treating a disease.

Step 2: Evaluation
Contraceptives are not regular biological requirements for reproductive maintenance; they are chosen to prevent, delay, or space pregnancies. Users should be aware of potential adverse effects such as nausea, abdominal cramps, breakthrough bleeding, irregular menstrual cycles, or rarely breast cancer, necessitating professional medical consultation.

Step 3: Final Answer
Contraceptives act against a natural reproductive event and can produce side effects such as nausea and irregular bleeding.

answer.text: Contraceptives are regular physiological requirements essential for the basal metabolic maintenance of reproductive health
Synthetic hormonal contraceptives are completely devoid of any potential risk or endocrine side effects
Contraceptives are practiced against a natural reproductive event and may cause side effects such as nausea, abdominal pain, breakthrough bleeding, and irregular menstrual bleeding
All contraceptive methods confer total lifelong immunity against reproductive tract cancers and systemic infections

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MCQ_Q48 - Societal indicators signifying improvement in community reproductive health

questiontext.text: Which comprehensive set of social and medical indicators signifies an improved reproductive health status in a society?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Community reproductive health is gauged through healthcare delivery metrics, educational awareness, and maternal-infant epidemiological indicators.

Step 2: Evaluation
Positive indicators of societal reproductive health include enhanced sex education, increased institutional and medically assisted deliveries, decreased maternal mortality rate (MMR) and infant mortality rate (IMR), better detection and treatment of STIs, and increased prevalence of smaller, healthy families.

Step 3: Final Answer
Improved reproductive health is indicated by enhanced awareness, more medically assisted deliveries, reduced MMR and IMR, and better STI management.

answer.text: Rising maternal and infant mortality rates along with an increased preference for unassisted home deliveries
A decrease in institutional deliveries and lack of sex education in school curricula
Complete absence of birth control options accompanied by an uncontrolled rise in family size
Increased awareness of sex-related matters, higher numbers of medically assisted deliveries, reduced maternal and infant mortality rates, and improved detection and treatment of STIs
